newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian bourse delists ailing Privredna Banka.
newsitem.headline: Croatian bourse delists ailing Privredna Banka.

text.p: Croatia's central bourse, the Zagreb Stock Exchange, said on Thursday it had delisted ailing Privredna Banka to prevent trade in its stock while the bank is being recapitalised.
Anyone buying Privredna's shares now with a hope of making money when it is healthy again was cautioned that the present ownership structure or values may not be preserved.
"For all practical purposes these shares do not exist. If they are replaced by new ones at a later stage, they can be listed again," spokesman Zeljko Kardum told Reuters.
Privredna's stock was traded in the semi-regulated bourse segment with minimum listing requirements and an over-the-counter (OTC) market in Varazdin.

But all outstanding shares in the bank, the country's largest, were withdrawn when the government decided to overhaul it last year. The decision was published in the official gazette Narodne Novine on December 17.
Since there was no explicit ban on trade at the time, some deals have indeed been made both on the bourse and OTC market.
"Brokers probably did not read the decision (on the overhaul)," said one trader. "Some guidelines would have been helpful."
The state securities commission declined any comment on these developments although it admitted being aware of them.
Several months after three commissioners were appointed to head the market watchdog, it still has no other staff or instruments to steer and supervise the market.
But one source speaking on condition of anonymity told Reuters the issuer and the bourse had been contacted to straighten out the tangle.
As a result the bourse annulled last week's deals involving some 7,000 Privredna shares sold at 260 kuna, Kardum said.
The Varazdin OTC market, which is governed by less strict rules, plans no move to annul trade unless buyers and sellers agree to it, according to its director Marijan Cingula.
The fact that all was not quite right became obvious when the bank refused to enter new owners in the shareholder book.

Privredna said it was a direct result of the government's plans with it, according to which all shares will eventually be reissued at an as yet uncertain price to reflect a new capital value and structure.
"The shareholder register has been temporarily closed and will remain closed until then," said official Ivan Krolo. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
